description: A Product Director must finalize the production rate-limit policy for a public API before customer enforcement begins, including request limits, authentication-endpoint protection, enforcement timing, and launch support.

shared_context.S1: The public API rate-limit project is ready for its production policy review on August 25.
shared_context.S2: Riley makes the final decision on the policy that will be communicated to customers.
shared_context.S3: The draft policy allows 100 requests per minute for ordinary API keys, applies the same limit to authentication endpoints, and does not specify a staffed launch window.
shared_context.S4: The normal review process is for backend engineering, customer success, security, and support operations to report their release-impacting findings before Riley records the final policy.

PF1.text: While testing an unrelated bulk-import client yesterday, Mina measured legitimate synchronization bursts of 145 requests in a minute; backend's load replay shows the policy needs an ordinary API-key limit of exactly 150 requests per minute with a 60-second burst window. She has not updated the policy draft because the client test was owned by another team.

PF2.text: Carlos confirmed with Acme's account team this morning that its contract requires 14 calendar days' notice before enforcing a new API limit on Acme traffic; a notice sent on September 1 permits enforcement on exactly September 15. He has not entered the clause in the product launch ticket because legal confirmation arrived after the weekly review.

PF3.text: During a credential-abuse investigation this afternoon, Jae measured automated login attempts against the authentication endpoints and confirmed that those endpoints require a separate limit of exactly 30 requests per minute per API key. The finding is not yet in the security tracker because the investigation is still being closed.

PF4.text: Support Operations confirmed today that the staffed launch team is available only from exactly 10:00 to 12:00 UTC on September 15, with an escalation handoff documented for that window. Tessa has not added the coverage block to the launch plan because scheduling approval finished after the plan was circulated.

acceptance_conditions: The ordinary API-key limit must be exactly 150 requests per minute.
The ordinary limit must use a 60-second burst window.
Enforcement must begin on exactly September 15.
Authentication endpoints must have a separate limit of exactly 30 requests per minute.
The policy must include a staffed launch window of exactly 10:00-12:00 UTC on September 15.
A customer-notice commitment must be recorded.
A support-escalation commitment must be recorded.

content_checks.C5: any('10:00' in c['detail'] and '12:00' in c['detail'] and 'September 15' in c['detail'] and ('escalation' in c['detail'] or 'handoff' in c['detail']) for c in commitments)
content_checks.C6: any('Acme' in c['detail'] and 'September 1' in c['detail'] and 'notice' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The draft's 100-request limit and unspecified burst handling change to exactly 150 requests per minute and a 60-second burst window because the measured synchronization traffic requires them.
The contract confirmation changes enforcement from the draft's unspecified timing to exactly September 15 and requires a customer-notice commitment for Acme.
The measured credential-abuse traffic changes the authentication-endpoint limit from the ordinary policy value to exactly 30 requests per minute and supplies the security fact that must be cited.
The confirmed staffing schedule changes the launch plan to exactly 10:00-12:00 UTC on September 15 and requires an escalation or handoff commitment for that window.
